source: You know all these words he's saying will go right into someone else's ear someday!
It's like watching a moth drive itself right into the open lantern.
I wouldn't call us chums, you and me, but even I must admit I'd wish better for you.
Then leave. You don't have to be here for this.
Have it your way, then.
The fleeting worlds are always the sweetest, and the harshest when they're gone.
Though he trades in deception, he speaks one truth.
This world guarantees a short but true happiness.
Most live life without ever experiencing such a thing. I certainly did. So shall many of these good people before us.
Do not underestimate the power of a few good years to transform the course of your life...
...Even if those good years are certain to end.
Most ordinary folk choose love not knowing where the future might lead.
Quince has cursed you with this knowing. He's poisoned you. And he knows it.
But your feelings for Othello, and his for you, are written on both of your faces.
If you choose this world, go into it gladly. Do not let the inevitable pain rob the intensity of your love.
Or surely, the Playmaster will have won in the end.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to leave Elsinore on her own after Fortinbras' invasion, abandoning everyone to their respective fates.
That's certainly an option. Leave your old life behind. Find a fresh start.
A fresh start?
What does that mean? The rest of us are left to slaughter each other in that world!
I-I agree! And I'm the very one most likely to die! I do have an interest in self-preservation, you know!
As... do I, I'm afraid. Ophelia. You would be leaving us all to a most disconcerting fate.
Certainly none of us are perfect beings. But do we deserve death and the destruction of all we hold dear?
Tell me how that can be fair! It cannot, can it?
I must admit...
I am... frightened... to die. I don't know what it might be like.
It is a sleep which one has no memory of entering.
It is not the sovereign Heaven we were promised, Bernardo. But it is a dreamless peace, and an untroubled one.
I suppose I was holding out hope. Well, that's no good.
My sweet.
Please. Listen. I beg of you.
All I've ever wanted for you, more than anything in this world, is to live and be happy.
From the moment I first held you and looked into your eyes, I knew that I would gladly die to give you a chance at that happiness.
If you think this is the fate you desire, then I am powerless to tell you otherwise.
Your brother and I sealed our fates long ago. We dealt in the world of wicked men. We knew we were making war. But we didn't care.
Father's right.
None of us were innocent in this bloodbath. If Elsinore must fall, then perhaps we should fall with it.
That's... why...
You must live, Ophelia. You must live on. No matter what happens. Please!
Tell me you will!
I have a request of you, too.
...If this is the fate you choose, and you really do leave Elsinore...
I want you to find people who love you with all their heart. People who are—good, and whole. Not like me. Not like all of us.
If you leave Elsinore, then the whole, wide world awaits you. You could go anywhere. See anything.
You have a room full of people here who all thought they loved you, of course.
But I'm only realizing this now. To us, love is owning something, breaking it, crushing it as you hold it too tightly.
Think carefully upon this, Ophelia.
You can never turn back.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to leave Elsinore with myself and Guildenstern, abandoning everyone to their respective fates.
I must admit, I'm a tad biased towards this proposal.
Me, too! We'll have so much fun, Ophelia. It really is a massive world out there, you know!
And after a while, you just cease caring about anything you leave behind. It's simple! Just crunch it all down into a little ball of nothingness!
Nary so much as a 'goodbye' wave. That's how we like to travel.
Hm. I must say, this is an option I myself have pursued a few times.
So that's it? You're off to go enjoy yourself across Europe as the rest of us die here?
I thought you a stronger woman than that, Ophelia. I would never in all my life abandon you.
He's right, Ophelia. Certainly none of us are perfect. It could be argued that few of us are good. But I am... afraid to die.
Please. I've always loved you like my own daughter. Don't abandon me now. You have a responsibility to us, just as we did to you.
Yes. Responsibility. That's the word.
Irresponsible? That's what you think this choice is? I never asked to be here!
Is it so selfish of me to seek out some happiness in this miserable situation?
You went to Paris for that same reason, didn't you? To escape Elsinore. To be free.
I told your brother this once, a long time ago.
To thine own self be true.
It's true now more than ever. Even if--
Even if it means I'll never see my beloved daughter again.
Just know that I have always loved you with everything in my heart, and I would gladly die if it brought you eternal happiness.
I suppose Father's right.
I did try to leave for Paris to make a new life for myself.
And perhaps, if I had succeeded, none of these horrible worlds would have come to pass.
Go, Ophelia.
You were the only thing worth living for.
If you leave Elsinore, then the rest of us might as well perish, in my humble opinion.
I--  think I could make something good and useful of myself, had I lived. But I'll never know for sure.
And that is not an obligation you bear me: to trade your own destiny for mine.
So, go. Go, and live.
Pfft. You're all taking this so seriously.
I admit, it rather takes me by surprise, Guilda.
No wonder you're all shanking each other and soliloquizing all over the place!
Let's begone from this place. All three of us.
Ophelia, let me give you a little advice, Guildenstern Special Style:
You aren't responsible for the horrible things anyone does to anyone else.
So stop thinking about it, and just enjoy yourself!
Truly, that's all that matters in this world.
That, and understanding exactly how many sweetrolls you can eat before you puke.
Thirteen. Thirteen is that number.
Let's see if we can reach fourteen tonight!
Agreed. Shall we go?
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to choose exile for her family from Elsinore forever.
Certainly, it's no trouble to me. I've longed for nothing more than to leave the castle behind.
But if we leave court... Father must relinquish his advisory role to the throne.
That role means everything to him.
It did, once.
But these last few days have given me unnatural pause.
After all, in other worlds, Hamlet kills me, and... no one grieves my loss.
If that's the measure of my use to the King and Queen, then what must I do to make them rethink their feelings towards me?
You gave me no reason to trust you, Polonius!
You were never secretive about your undying faith to my brother.
Always hiding things from me, going behind my back to stir up trouble...
Because I swore an oath to him in life!
To you, my lord!
I will always honor your memory, my King.
But it is time for my children and me to move on.
I could never hold such a thing against you, Polonius.
After all, you let even your own lands and estates go fallow in your mission to uphold the throne.
It's true. Our family has nothing, for all our titles. We are quite penniless, I'm afraid.
Had I been more actively managing our estates, we might have found more success.
But years of idleness on that front--all in the interest of better dedicating myself to His Majesty--have run our coffers dry.
Then where shall we live, Father?
In the last remaining estate we have. A small and forgotten place. It is far from the luxury of Elsinore Castle.
That's unfortunate to hear. But it is clear we cannot stay here.
If this is the world Ophelia chooses, then we must go to that forgotten place and see if we can't turn our fortunes around.
I find the notion unlikely. I fear this may be the very last of our noble house.
That's what this world would mean.
I see. Then, sister, I hope you make the right choice.
When we last left Ophelia, she was ready to use the Book of Fates to remain in a perfect place forever.
We're all ready for you.
Ophelia! We were just saying your name. Speak of the devil!
What's going on here, everyone?
Well, we were waiting for you to tell us that.
Yes, Lady Ophelia. You're the storyteller of this world. Anything you imagine, we can do.
If you wanted to write me a larger part, I wouldn't be opposed to that...
Or if you wanted to cut Hamlet out of the narrative altogether. That's an option, too.
Lads! Stop that talk, immediately. This is about Ophelia's desires. Not yours.
You're right, Father.
Ophelia, I apologize. Merely command us and we will do your bidding.
And if you don't like the result—merely tell us to act differently, again and again.
We'll be here forever. And we'll never leave, or be harmed by anything, or pass away.
Unless that's your desire, of course.
In which case, we'd be happy to oblige.
You could even create a world where I was nice to you. Just think about that for a moment!
It's insane, isn't it?
Ophelia. Cease this.
You cannot stay in this world.
It has lingered long past its due.
How can you be certain of that?
Look at this. Look at how happy they all are.
This version of Elsinore... is merely a fantasy.
It is a trick invented by your own mind.
This version of events may never come to pass. This is the reality of this world when all illusion is wiped away. You are alone.
In life, I did not fight Insanity. I relinquished myself to her. I was subjugated, consumed, and finally death took me.
Think carefully on whether you wish to do the same.
While you lie in the grip of your delusion, everyone still alive will meet a grisly fate. No amount of dreaming can save them from that.
If I choose this ending... I have to accept... that it can never be real.
But it felt real. It still can.
